faq: What is the main difference between a job description and a job specification? → A job description explains the role: its duties, responsibilities, and scope. What comes first, the job description or the job specification? → Write the job description first. It defines the work, and the specification is built from it: for every responsibility you list, you decide what skills and experience a person needs to deliver it. Doing it in that order keeps the two documents consistent.

Can a job description and job specification be in the same document? → Yes. Many teams combine them into one role profile, with the description on top and the specification below. Keep the two sections clearly separated so the public duties do not get tangled with the internal hiring criteria.

What should a job specification include? → It should list the required hard skills, the soft skills that predict success, a realistic experience range, any genuinely required education or certifications, and a clear split between must-have and nice-to-have. Ideally each must-have is tied to a way you will actually measure it.

How does a job specification support skills-based hiring? → The specification is where skills-based hiring starts. Every must-have skill it names can be turned into an assessment, so you screen people on what they can do rather than where they studied. faq: Is AI proctoring better than human proctoring? → Not always. AI proctoring is better for scale and consistency, while human proctoring is better for context, live oversight, and fair review in high-stakes exams.
What is hybrid proctoring? → Hybrid proctoring combines AI monitoring with human review. AI flags unusual activity, and trained reviewers check the context before a final decision is made.
Can AI proctoring create false positives? → Yes. AI can flag normal behavior, technical issues, or brief distractions as suspicious, which is why human review is important before taking action.
When should you use live human proctoring? → Use live human proctoring for high-stakes exams, certifications, or assessments where real-time intervention and human judgment matter more than scale.
Does AI proctoring still need human review? → Yes. AI is useful for monitoring and flagging risk, but serious exam integrity decisions are more accurate and fair when reviewed by humans.
